title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the specific study nooks, late-night tea houses, and creative hubs where Colorado College students actually spend their time between blocks.

cards.title: Sacred Grounds Tea House
cards.subtitle: Shove Memorial Chapel Lower Level
cards.notes: Visit this student-led, substance-free space for late-night tea and open mic nights. It is a cozy alternative to the library for evening study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A student-run late-night tea house and study space located in the basement of Shove Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacred Grounds is a student-led late-night gathering space open from 9pm-12am Wednesday-Saturday, serving as a substance-free venue and study space.
cards.access_notes: Open late night 9 PM to 12 AM, Wednesday through Saturday.

cards.title: The Bean Table
cards.subtitle: Behind McGregor Hall
cards.notes: Head to this bean-shaped outdoor table for a quiet sunset view of Pikes Peak. It is a favorite spot for solo reflection or small group discussions.
cards.short_summary: A signature bean-shaped outdoor table behind McGregor Hall known for its mountain views.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ritt Kellogg Table, often called the 'bean table,' is a student-favorite spot behind McGregor Hall for watching sunsets and reflecting.

cards.title: The Fourth Floor 'Fishbowl'
cards.subtitle: Charles L. Tutt Library
cards.notes: Grab a seat in the glass-walled rooms on the top floor for panoramic mountain views. These spaces are highly sought after during finals week.
cards.short_summary: High-visibility glass study rooms on the top floor of the library offering expansive views.
cards.evidence_claim: Students favor the 'window rooms' or 'fishbowl' areas in Tutt Library for the views of the mountains and sunsets.
cards.source_title: Charles L. Tutt Library Self-Guided Tour
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary; typically open late for students with card access.

cards.title: Cornerstone Main Space
cards.subtitle: Cornerstone Arts Center
cards.notes: Use this multi-level atrium for informal socializing or catching pop-up student performances. The architecture itself serves as a stage.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, open atrium in the arts center used for studying, socializing, and impromptu events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cornerstone Main Space is used for performances, classes, or informal socializing and features an innovative layout.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; often used for late-night rehearsals.

cards.title: Ritt Kellogg Climbing Gym
cards.subtitle: Adam F. Press Fitness Center Lower Level
cards.notes: Practice bouldering or top-roping at this free student gym. Equipment is provided, making it an easy spot to de-stress between classes.
cards.short_summary: A 3,500 square-foot indoor climbing facility located within the campus fitness center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ritt Kellogg Climbing Gym is a free indoor rock climbing gym for students with equipment provided.
cards.access_notes: Requires active Gold Card for free student access.

cards.title: Worner Arts & Crafts Studios
cards.subtitle: Worner Campus Center
cards.notes: Join a non-graded class in ceramics, fiber arts, or metal. It is a popular creative outlet for students looking to work with their hands.
cards.short_summary: Student-accessible studios for creative projects outside of the formal academic curriculum.
cards.evidence_claim: Worner Campus Center is home to the Arts & Crafts program studios offering classes in ceramics, fiber arts, and metal.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 8:30 AM - 8:00 PM; weekend hours vary.

cards.title: Olin Hall Fishbowl
cards.subtitle: Olin Hall of Science
cards.notes: Study in this glass-enclosed space within the science building. It is known for being a quiet, focused environment for STEM students.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet study area in the science building characterized by its glass walls.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'fishbowl' in Olin Hall is listed as a student favorite study spot on campus.

cards.title: The Labyrinth
cards.subtitle: Outside Shove Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Walk this stone path for a meditative break. It is a quiet outdoor corner often used by students for mindfulness between intense blocks.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor meditative walking path located on the grounds of Shove Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: The labyrinth outside Shove Chapel is identified as a quiet corner and spiritual space for the CC community.

cards.title: The Preserve
cards.subtitle: Western Ridge Apartments
cards.notes: Escape the main dining hall for a quiet afternoon study break. This cafe-grocery hybrid is a favorite for its made-to-order specials.
cards.short_summary: A gourmet cafe and grocery space located in the Western Ridge residential area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Preserve is described as a perfect place for a quiet afternoon study break or weekend gathering.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check dining services for specific block break hours.

cards.title: Honnen 3D Arts Studio
cards.subtitle: 30 W. Cache La Poudre St.
cards.notes: Explore this former ice arena now transformed into a vibrant 3D arts hub. It houses sculpture and installation spaces for student projects.
cards.short_summary: A repurposed ice arena that now serves as the primary facility for 3D arts and sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Honnen Ice Arena was renovated in 2023 to become the home for the college's 3D Arts department.
cards.source_title: From Ice to Art: Honnen Ice Arena Undergoes Transformation
cards.access_notes: Primarily for art students; exhibitions are often open to the campus community.
